APA-formatted correlation table

Source: R/tables.R
apa_cor.Rd

APA-formatted correlation table

Usage

apa_cor(
  data,
  note = NULL,
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  digits = 2,
  bold_significant = FALSE,
  star_significant = TRUE,
  significance_note = TRUE,
  output = c("flextable", "tibble"),
  font_family = NULL,
  font_size = NULL,
  text_color = "black",
  border_color = "black",
  border_width = 0.5,
  line_spacing = NULL,
  table_width = NULL,
  keep_empty_star_columns = TRUE,
  summary_functions = list(M = mean, SD = stats::sd),
  column_formats = NULL,
  method = "pearson",
  p_adjust = "none",
  partial = FALSE,
  ...,
  p_value
)

Arguments

data

data.frame or tibble with variables to be correlated, or the output of correlation::correlation() (see Details)

note

note placed below the table, replacing the automatic note (for output = "flextable")

alpha

p-value thresholds for significance stars, from largest to smallest (default: c(.05, .01, .001), for one, two, and three stars). With bold_significant = TRUE, only the first is used.

digits

number of decimal places of the correlations (unaffected by apa7_defaults(accuracy = ))

bold_significant

if TRUE, correlations with p below the first alpha are bolded instead of starred. If FALSE (default), they are not.

star_significant

if TRUE (default), significant correlations get stars (one for each alpha they are below). Ignored when bold_significant = TRUE. Model tables such as apa_parameters() do the same with their starred and bolded arguments.

significance_note

if TRUE (default), the note explains the stars (or the bolding) when any correlation is significant

output

"flextable" (default) for a formatted table, or "tibble" for a tibble of the formatted values (without a note)

font_family

font family (e.g., "Times New Roman" or "Arial"). If NULL (default), the font set with apa7_defaults(font_family = ) (Times New Roman unless changed).

font_size

font size, in points. If NULL (default), the size set with apa7_defaults(font_size = ) (12 unless changed).

text_color

color of the text: an R color name (e.g., "black", the default) or a hex code (e.g., "#333333")

border_color

color of the rules, in the same forms as text_color

border_width

width of the rules, in points (default: 0.5)

line_spacing

spacing between lines of the header and body (e.g., 2 for double spacing or 1 for single spacing). If NULL (default), the spacing set with apa7_defaults(line_spacing = ) (2 unless changed). Table notes are single-spaced.

table_width

width of the table, in the same forms in every apa7 function: a proportion from 0 to 1 of the default width (the full width of a portrait page unless changed with apa7_defaults(table_width = )), "page" (or "portrait") for the full width of a portrait page, "landscape" for a landscape page, "column" for one column of a two-column page, or a named number: a proportion of one of these widths (e.g., c(landscape = .8)) or a width in inches, cm, or mm (e.g., c(inches = 5)). With 0, the columns are only as wide as their contents need. If NULL (default), the width set by the code chunk's apa7-width option in Quarto (e.g., #| apa7-width: landscape, or #| apa7-width: {landscape: .8} for a named number) or apa7.width option in R Markdown, or "page" for a chunk with apaquarto's apa-twocolumn: true; otherwise, the table_width set with apa7_defaults() (1 unless changed). The widths of the pages and the column are set with the page_width, landscape_width, and column_width arguments of apa7_defaults(). A number greater than 1 is read as inches, with a warning to write it as c(inches = ).

keep_empty_star_columns

if TRUE (default), every correlation column keeps its star column, even when no correlation in it is significant, so that the columns have the same width. If FALSE, empty star columns are removed.

summary_functions

Any named list of functions that summarize data columns (e.g., list(Mean = mean, SD = sd)). Can also be a character vector of function names (e.g., c("n", "M", "SD")). Functions available in a character vector: IQR, Interquartile Range, Kurtosis, MAD, Median Absolute Deviation, M, Mean, Med, Median, n, N, Quantile, Range, SD, Skewness, Var, Variance

column_formats

column_formats() object. If NULL (default), the default column formats are used.

method

kind of correlation (e.g., "pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "biweight", or "percentage"), passed to correlation::correlation(). Not used for correlation::correlation() output.

p_adjust

method of adjusting the p-values (and so the stars) for multiple comparisons (e.g., "holm", "bonferroni", or "fdr"). Unlike correlation::correlation(), the default is "none". Not used for correlation::correlation() output.

partial

if TRUE, partial correlations, each controlling for all other variables in the table. Not used for correlation::correlation() output.

...

other arguments passed to correlation::correlation() (e.g., robust = TRUE, winsorize = .2, or multilevel = TRUE). Not used for correlation::correlation() output.

p_value

deprecated; use alpha

Value

flextable::flextable

Details

apa_cor() computes the correlations with correlation::correlation(). By default, they are Pearson correlations of all pairwise complete observations, and the stars are for unadjusted p-values. Use method, p_adjust, partial, and the other arguments of correlation::correlation() for other kinds of correlations. The column names of data are the variable names in the table, and they can contain spaces and symbols (e.g., "Reading comprehension") for every kind of correlation: apa_cor() gives the variables internal names while the correlations are computed. Logical columns are correlated as 0 and 1.

The output of correlation::correlation() can also be passed as data. The table shows its correlations and p-values, and the summary columns are computed from the data that correlation::correlation() keeps with its results. Note that correlation::correlation() uses Holm's method by default, so the stars are for adjusted p-values unless p_adjust = "none", and that its partial and multilevel correlations do not accept variable names with spaces. For those, use apa_cor(data, partial = TRUE) instead.

The note says what kind of correlations are shown (unless they are ordinary Pearson correlations) and how the p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons. Correlations computed by group, between two sets of variables, or with Bayesian methods are not yet supported.

In apa7 0.2.0 and earlier, apa_cor() computed the correlations with psych::corTest(). Its adjust argument is still accepted as p_adjust, with a warning, and use = "complete" removes incomplete rows, with a warning.

# Partial Spearman correlations, with variable names that have spaces
d <- mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")]
names(d) <- c("Miles per gallon", "Weight (1000 lbs)", "Gross horsepower")
apa_cor(d, method = "spearman", partial = TRUE)
